extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to Nature Cell Biology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the journal's editorial process and peer-review expectations for manuscripts submitted to Nature Cell Biology, including decision criteria, reviewer selection, revision requirements, appeals, and transfer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial quality and completeness check
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript and associated materials are checked for quality and completeness by the journal’s editorial assistant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the journal's guidelines for initial submission to make sure you provide all necessary information at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances understanding of the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors decide whether to send a manuscript for peer review based on the degree to which it advances our understanding of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors read the paper and consult with the editorial team; on occasion they may consult expert researchers when deciding whether to review a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors assess the soundness of the manuscript's conclusions when deciding whether to send it for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment is part of the editor's read and consultation with the editorial team prior to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence supports conclusions (data and analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors consider the extent to which the evidence presented — including appropriate data and analyses — supports the manuscript's conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors evaluate whether the data and analyses are appropriate and sufficient to underpin the claims made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide relevance to the journal's readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors consider the wide relevance of the manuscript's conclusions to the journal’s readership when deciding whether to send it for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance to the journal audience is a factor alongside scientific advance and soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial consultation and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about whether to send a manuscript to peer review and final editorial decisions are made by the editor and the editorial team (no external editorial board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may consult with expert researchers on occasion; the editorial team discusses reviewer reports when making final publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection aims to ensure that the different technical and conceptual aspects of the work are covered by reviewers with relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer selection is critical; editors work hard to identify reviewers whose expertise matches the manuscript's technical and conceptual components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest reviewers; these suggestions are often helpful but are not always followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers can be taken into account, but editors retain discretion over reviewer invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not identified to the authors, except at the request of the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The default is that reviewer identities remain confidential unless a reviewer explicitly asks to be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision outcomes: invite to revise or decline
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewer reports are received, editors will either invite authors to revise and resubmit to address concerns or decline publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declines are typically on grounds of insufficient support for the conclusions or a reassessment of the level of interest or advance in light of reviewers' comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and resubmit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If invited to revise and resubmit, authors must provide a revised manuscript that addresses the issues raised, a response to each reviewer point, and a cover letter with any additional information requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the revised manuscript using the link provided in the decision email (do not submit as a new manuscript). Provide a point-by-point response to reviewer reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals (requests to reconsider a rejection) are considered secondary to normal submissions and are successful only if the editors are convinced the original decision was an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further consideration may be merited if a reviewer made substantial errors of fact or there is significant evidence of bias, but only if reversing that reviewer's opinion would have changed the original decision. If an appeal merits further consideration, editors may send authors' responses or the revised paper to reviewers or seek additional reviewer advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer option within Nature Portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: If Nature Cell Biology declines a manuscript, authors can transfer their manuscript (including reviewer comments) to another journal within the Nature Portfolio via the link in the decision email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This service is available at decision time or later. If assessed by the receiving journal as a good fit and technically sound, it may be accepted without further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of peer-review reports and identity sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a manuscript is transferred, the original reviewer reports and identities will be shared with the receiving journal, with exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers to the npj Series and Scientific Reports are exceptions (reports/identities not shared). If authors do not want the Nature Cell Biology review history shared, they should not use the transfer service and must instead make a new submission; this decision must be made at the time of initial submission and cannot be changed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when transferring a peer-reviewed manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript has been peer-reviewed and is transferred, authors should include a note explaining any changes made to the manuscript compared to the original Nature Cell Biology submission, along with a separate point-by-point response to the reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear explanation of changes and a point-by-point response to help the receiving journal take the previous review into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Received date for transferred publications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of publication after transfer, the received date is the date of submission to the journal where the manuscript is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The received date reflects submission to the final publishing journal, not the original submission to Nature Cell Biology.
